sub_bullets: Z47^fortyseven moved +2.4% over the month versus Nifty 500’s +2.2%, finishing 0.2 percentage points ahead.
Z47^fortyseven kept pace with the broader market despite a tougher macro backdrop, with its domestic-demand orientation continuing to cushion global cyclical pressures.
SaaS/AI was the best-performing sector in the cohort at +8.2%, while Fintech was the weakest at +1.3%, reflecting growing investor interest in AI-linked businesses.

sections.header: Largest constituents ; the names that anchor the index
sub_bullets: Eternal (Zomato) +5.1%; continued reinvestment in quick commerce weighed on near-term sentiment; Blinkit delivered its first profitable quarter.
Groww +9.8%; strong broking and margin-trading momentum supported performance; elevated valuations moderated further gains.
Lenskart +2.5%; continued store densification and margin expansion kept it among the stronger-performing large-weight constituents.
CarTrade +29.3%; strong execution in its consumer auto marketplace and a cash-rich balance sheet supported sustained investor interest.
RateGain +25.2%; moved with the broader cohort this month.
Meesho -14.1%; moved with the broader cohort this month.
PolicyBazaar -14.1%; moved with the broader cohort this month.
Operating performance best captures the cohort's underlying progress this quarter; reported profit was shaped by one-off items and reinvestment.
Profit growth outpaced revenue across the cohort, reflecting improving operating leverage as businesses scaled.
AI is emerging as both a cost lever and a growth lever; the more significant value creation is coming from businesses using it to reshape demand, not just improve efficiency.
The lending cohort grew earnings while improving asset quality, as stronger underwriting discipline drove a more resilient growth profile.
Cash generation is increasingly defining success across the cohort, letting market leaders fund acquisitions and expansion from their own balance sheets.
Supply rotation from foreign VC exits to domestic institutional demand continued; large block sales cleared without dislocation, and ownership is becoming structural rather than flow-driven.
Global headwinds (oil, a softer rupee, rate-cut delay, monsoon risk) persist, but continued digital adoption across India remains a meaningful offset for much of the cohort.
The cohort absorbed significant institutional supply without meaningful market dislocation.
Performance dispersion widened, with profitability and earnings quality increasingly distinguishing the strongest performers from the rest.
